title: Steering rules are data that a test enforces

statements.says: The rules for where code goes and how it is commented live in two files, a file-placement rules file and a comments rules file.
An architecture test project reads the YAML block in each rules file and fails when the code breaks it.
Changing a rule means editing one of those two files and nothing else.
The rule on whether a // comment is worth keeping stays as text, and /comment-sweep cleans up what the text misses.

The spec loop runs the sweep and the review as its own steps, in one session through claude -p --resume: /implement N --stop-after-tests, then /comment-sweep, then /code-review with the commit and the close.
Run by hand with no flag, /implement still does every step itself.
The existing code is restructured before or with the test, never after.
The restructure brings feature folders then concern folders, one type per file, namespaces that match folders, and test folders that mirror source folders.
The front end moves from layer first to feature first, so the paths in .dependency-cruiser.cjs change once.
The loop keeps the plain-words output style, renamed skillworks.
skillworks-setup writes the output style to .claude/output-styles/ and sets it in .claude/settings.json when no style is set.
Claude puts too many files in one folder, too many types in one file, and too many comments in both.
Written rules alone do not stop it: a comment rule held on 10 runs of 15.
859 of the repo's comment lines were XML doc comments that no build reads.
A folder shape and the presence of a doc comment are facts, so a test can decide them.
Whether a // comment is worth keeping is not a fact, so a test cannot decide it.
A test runs where /implement already has to pass the full suite before it can close a ticket.
A step written into a skill can be skipped, and a step in the script cannot.
The existing code breaks the rules, which is why it has to be restructured.
A PreToolUse hook was rejected, because it fires on every write, blocks the half-moved state of any restructure, and never sees a git mv run from Bash.
Text only was rejected, because the flat folders already in this repo are what text alone produced.

An output style with keep-coding-instructions: false was rejected, because although it scored 15 of 15 on comment density it also drops Claude Code's instructions on scope and verification, and nobody has priced that.
The output style with keep-coding-instructions: false is also not needed, because the doc comment check covers what it fixed.

The sentence saying the spec loop runs the sweep and the review as its own steps in one session is superseded by a later record: the loop now runs seven steps, the review is three of them, and each runs in a session of its own, while the other two sentences of that paragraph stand.
